public_rationale: The controlled scaling study available in June 2024 documented predictable performance gains across model sizes and training amounts [e1]. The May 2023 data-constrained study found diminishing returns from repeatedly reusing limited data, establishing a limit within that experimental setting [e2]. Neither study establishes a fundamental ceiling below trustworthy general intelligence [e1, e2]. The June 2026 version of the capability study examined task-dependent saturation using models with contemporary post-training, so it does not isolate scaling alone [e3]. These studies establish neither the required lasting ceiling nor a scaling-only achievement of trustworthy general intelligence, leaving the forecast unresolved [e1, e2, e3].
limitations: The claim specifies no deadline, capability threshold, or operational test of trustworthy general intelligence.
Finite experiments and task-specific saturation do not establish a universal ceiling.
The boundary between scaling and other training improvements remains unspecified.
The absence of a qualifying demonstration does not establish that scaling alone must fail.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scaling alone will prove useful only up to a point.

statement.excerpt: “Scaling” alone—building bigger and models until they absorb the entire internet — will prove useful, but only to a point.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

our_interpretation: Scaling means increasing language-model size and pretraining data or compute, without adding qualitatively different reasoning tools or system components.
In the surrounding discussion, only to a point means that scaling improves capabilities but is insufficient by itself for trustworthy general intelligence.
A temporary benchmark plateau, diminishing returns, or current model failures do not alone establish that lasting limit.
Scaling alone specifies the development regime to assess. Controlled scaling experiments establish that this regime has been attempted.
The nearby decade and 2043 predictions concern other propositions and are not imported as this claim's deadline.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes useful gains from scaling and a persistent limitation preventing scaling alone from reaching trustworthy general intelligence, rather than merely showing finite experimental saturation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A transparently documented system developed through scaling alone demonstrably achieves trustworthy general intelligence under broad, credible independent evaluation.

evidence.explanation: The researchers report a controlled testbed varying model size and training tokens, establishing that the scaling regime was attempted. Predictable gains within that testbed also caution against treating scaling as already exhausted.

The study finds saturation when compute is added while repeatedly reusing constrained data. That is evidence of a specific scaling limit, not a demonstration that scaling model size and additional data cannot reach trustworthy general intelligence.

This recent study examines capability boundaries and saturation across benchmarks. Its observational comparisons include contemporary post-training, so they cannot determine the ultimate effect of scaling alone.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A validated result establishing a fundamental ceiling that prevents scaling alone from achieving trustworthy general intelligence, or a transparently documented scaling-only system independently shown to achieve it. Either requires an operational definition and evidence separating scale from other development changes.
